entries.reason: An animal is drawn as the engine's primitive of its slot, coloured by the pack's swatch for the family, until an animal catalog with rigged bodies exists; a pack may not dress it with a static mesh.

entries.reason: A fence, hedge or wall run repeats a module along its length, ends trimmed, so any run length is dressed without stretching. A pack may instead colour the engine's own piece with the family's swatch.

entries.reason: A person's look comes from the published character catalogs and the character studio; a pack names catalog looks or an outfit palette, never a mesh of its own.

entries.reason: A door module fills its opening so no hole shows round it; it may stretch on each axis only within the bounds below of its authored size, else the next variant or the fallback is drawn. A filled module is drawn when each axis of the slot lies from 800 to 1,250 per mille of the module's authored size, so an opening is never filled by a module stretched past a quarter or squeezed past a fifth. A pack may instead colour the engine's own piece with the family's swatch.

entries.reason: A bed, a bench or a workbench is scaled uniformly into its slot with its base on the floor, so its proportions hold. A pack may instead colour the engine's own piece with the family's swatch.
